brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A base that holds removable bins for small parts (at least two bins)
requirements.evidence: Two removable bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (full-depth, 2 compartments) in the full base, and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-half-n-full-div2 in the north half base. Both drop into their cells.

requirements.requirement: At least one drawer in the base
requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,1#cut (classic style) on the cut face of the north half base at 0,1.

requirements.requirement: A carry handle on the organizer
requirements.evidence: handle:0,0,0;top on the top cover of the full base, with three inserts.

requirements.requirement: Portable: a compact build, kept under about 30 parts
requirements.evidence: 18 parts: 2 pieces, 8 caps/covers, 2 bins, 1 drawer, 1 handle, 3 inserts, 1 joint bolt, 7 caps total counting the open faces (cover counted separately).

requirements.requirement: Build passes the configurator checks with no rule errors
requirements.evidence: check_build: ok, meshClash clear, no issues at all. Open cap faces were closed with 7 caps, so OPEN_CAP_FACE no longer appears.

finish.summary: Portable electronics organizer: two hex bases (a full base and a north half base) joined by a joint bolt. It holds two removable 2-compartment bins, one classic drawer on the half base's cut face, and a carry handle on the full base's top cover. All open cap faces are capped, and check_build is clean with mesh clear. Material, strength and handle load are not checked here.

lines.label: Bin, north half, full depth, 2 compartments
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
